Hemostasis

Some dental extraction reports find shorter bleeding times with blue or blue-violet light, while a tonsillectomy trial raises a possible bleeding concern. Evidence is sparse and setting-specific.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

Some dental extraction reports find shorter bleeding times with blue or blue-violet light, while a tonsillectomy trial raises a possible bleeding concern. Evidence is sparse and setting-specific.

Summary of the Evidence

Circulation > Hemostasis contains two records: one review and one rat protein analysis. Related records include two controlled blue/blue-violet LED extraction studies, one controlled LLLT extraction cohort in hemophilia, a 22-participant tonsillectomy RCT, and two related animal reports; these modalities and settings are not interchangeable. The 2020–2021 Arjmand rat publications appear to reuse plasma-protein data.

Human and clinical evidence

Extraction studies report shorter bleeding times, including a 22.42% reduction in a 60-patient hemophilia cohort. In contrast, a tonsillectomy RCT reported two hemostasis failures and raised possible postoperative bleeding risk (Koyi et al. 2025; Veleska-Stevkoska & Koneski, 2018; Kelkar et al., 2023; Celsi et al., 2022). Blue LED photocoagulation is distinct from red/NIR PBM.

Primary original studies: Veleska-Stevkoska and Koneski 2018 Koyi et al. 2025

Animal evidence

A hemophilic-mouse study reported faster wound closure and increased platelet procoagulant activity. The linked rat reports describe changes in fibrinogen/plasminogen-related proteins, not independent replications (Arjmand et al., 2020, 2021; Hoffman & Monroe, 2012).

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

none identified.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The extraction studies describe visible blue-violet LEDs at 410/470 nm or 480 nm; one report used 20 seconds of 480 nm exposure. The proposed local effect is photo-thermal clotting, which differs from low-dose PBM. Visible blue-violet light is distinct from near-infrared treatment, and results should not be transferred across procedures or mechanisms.

Interpretation

The findings apply to particular extraction sites and devices, not to systemic coagulation or all surgery. A faster local clot endpoint does not establish lower transfusion, reoperation, or complication rates. The tonsillectomy signal warrants treating surgical setting and modality as central to interpretation.

Evidence strength in source summaryVery low for general hemostasis. Small local-light studies differ by wavelength and surgical setting.
Publications and records7 unique titles: 2 exact-category and 5 narrowly related reports.

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

Small extraction studies report faster local bleeding control, including blue-violet LED approaches, while a hemophilia cohort evaluates another laser intervention. A tonsillectomy trial raises a possible postoperative bleeding concern. These settings and light mechanisms are not interchangeable, and the blue-light extraction work is photocoagulation rather than classic PBM.
